newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-HINGIS MARCHES ON, MAJOLI, NOVOTNA STRUGGLE THROUGH.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS MARCHES ON, MAJOLI, NOVOTNA STRUGGLE THROUGH.

text.p: Top seed Martina Hingis's charge toward a second grand slam title gathered momentum when she brushed past Sabine Appelmans of Belgium in straight sets to book her first quarter-final berth at Wimbledon on Tuesday.
Hingis, who became the youngest grand slam champion this century when she won the Australian Open earlier this year, has not dropped a set here and took just over an hour to beat Appelmans 6-1 6-3.

"I told her (Appelmans) after the match, 'Well I've got two more matches to go, so I want to keep it short' , that's why I played so well," said Hingis, who was scheduled to play two doubles matches later in the day.
Appelmans, ranked 19th in the world, dismissed suggestions that such comments bordered on arrogance.
"She's the number one player in the world," she said. "I think, without that attitude, maybe she wouldn't get so far."
The 16-year-old converted her first match point with a deft drop volley just as the first drops of rain fell, on another day of several interruptions due to the bad weather.
Fourth seed Iva Majoli of Croatia, the only player to beat Hingis in a singles match this year, survived a tight match with Romania's Irina Spirlea, the 12th seed, winning 6-7 6-1 9-7.
The French Open champion had not won a match on grass until her first round game here.
She will next meet Russian teenager Anna Kournikova who continued her startling run in her first Wimbledon, beating Helena Sukova -- who at 32 years is twice her age -- 2-6 6-2 6-3.
Third seed Jana Novotna was also stretched to a third set, for the third time in four matches, by 11th seed Mary Joe Fernandez.
"It was just a matter of guts and I was really going for it at the end...I feel like I have won Wimbledon already," said Novotna after her 5-7 6-4 7-5 win in two hours and nine minutes.
Novotna, who now meets unseeded Yayuk Basuki of Indonesia in the quarter-finals, said the media had unfairly labelled her "a choker" after surrendering to Steffi Graf in the 1993 Wimbledon final.
"I just don't see why people always get the wrong impression about me choking...I think that's totally wrong because I'm number three in the world," said the Czech born player.
Fernandez's exit left the women's tournament without an American in the last eight for the first time since 1946.
Hingis has a favourable draw and next meets unseeded Denisa Chladkova of the Czech Republic.

Eighth seed Aranxta Sanchez Vicario, runner-up here the last two years, breezed past ninth seeded Frenchwoman Mary Pierce in straight sets. The Spaniard will next play France's Nathalie Tauziat, ranked 22 in the world.
